acv.quote: Around ninety-five thousand a year. Ninety-five K ACV, on a two-year term.

data.reason: Martin, the CFO, saw only a side-by-side rate page. Nothing showed what failed orders cost Fernbrook. Sam blames price, but we never showed the value in their numbers.

trigger.action: Aim messaging at retailers losing big orders at checkout.
trigger.why: Lucy came inbound because one in twelve online orders failed at payment, worse on big baskets.
trigger.quote: one in twelve online orders was failing at the payment step

decider.action: Put the cost of failed orders in front of the finance decider.
decider.why: Martin decided from a rate-only page. Sam never met him, and Lucy carried our case alone.
decider.quote: Martin said no. Lucy told me. I never met him.

competitor.action: Prepare buyers for their bank cutting its rate to keep them.
competitor.why: Lucy said the bank offered only a better rate. After that her questions moved from declines to rate.
competitor.quote: After the bank came back, every email was the rate.

message.action: Keep explaining why big orders get declined and how we fix it.
message.why: Farah's explanation of big-ticket declines had Lucy nodding, but it never reached Martin.
message.quote: Lucy was nodding the whole way.

proof.action: Build a one-page business case a buyer can hand to finance.
proof.why: Lucy asked for one for Martin. Sam sent the deck, and Farah's decline analysis never ran.
proof.quote: something she could hand Martin. Like a one-page business case.

words.action: Say 'orders dying at the last step' instead of 'declines'.
words.why: Lucy described losing big baskets, like a four-thousand-dollar greenhouse, when the card says no.
words.quote: orders dying at the last step
